title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
content_md: Cisco Talos is tracking the growing in-the-wild usage of AI-enabled penetration testing frameworks. AI-enabled penetration testing and red team frameworks can automate and chain reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow-on actions, lowering the skill threshold for attackers and accelerating intrusions when the tools are misused. Talos has seen full automation of the attack chain by these frameworks, which not only use free and open-source tools, like nmap and nuclei, but also take advantage of internet mapping services like Censys and Shodan, CAPTCHA bypass services, credential leak management services, residential proxies, and even hash cracking services. This is the case of Hephaestus, which we mentioned in our previous report . Although these frameworks all have the same purpose, they come in different flavors. Some, like Hephaestus, are command line tools which can be deployed with a single script on a VPS and are completely controllable via Telegram. PentAGI has a web interface to monitor the agent activity with a full attack chain graph design and monitoring. Talos found more than 700 instances of currently reachable PentAGI instances on the internet. HexStrike AI integrates with many different clients like Claude Code, VS Code, or any other client that supports MCP.
